As an intern of the product management team, you will be an active contributor to the innovation and competitiveness of control system solutions for power plants around the world.

The Controls Product Management Intern will support the Product Management team in the end-to-end development and lifecycle management of our control system products.

We operate with a founder’s mindset. We deliver innovation with passion, speed, and courage. We continuously challenge our thinking and are empowered to dream big and take smart risks.

The intern will work closely with cross-functional teams, including engineering, supply chain, and marketing, to help define product vision, prioritize and track development, and ensure we are delivering maximum value to our customers.

- Conduct customer, market, and stakeholder discovery; synthesize qualitative and quantitative inputs to identify and prioritize unmet needs.

Job Summary

Inspire Vancouver is the City of Vancouver’s cultural access program. The program is a long-term investment in the organizations, people, and cultural life that make Vancouver a vibrant place to live. Funded by a .1% cultural access tax, the program supports arts, culture, heritage, and science organizations across the city.
The program is guided by four goals: expanding access and engagement, strengthening the cultural community, boosting jobs and neighborhood pride, and encouraging creativity and learning. The program is guided by the Culture, Arts and Heritage Commission, a body of nine community, and our grant review committee that is made up for Vancouver residents.
Inspire Vancouver places special emphasis on expanding access for people and communities who have historically faced barriers to participation. As a brand-new team, we’re building our programs and our evidence base at the same time, which is where you come in.

Job Details

We are looking for an intern to help launch our community measurement and learning practice. You will help design and conduct culturally responsive, engaging community surveys with three key audiences: the broader Vancouver community, our grantees, and the local artists, historians, scientists, and cultural leaders shaping Vancouver’s creative life. You’ll then turn that data into clear, compelling reports we can share with the community, the Culture, Arts and Heritage Commission, and the Vancouver City Council to demonstrate the impact of our grants and funding.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape the data story of a new public program. Your work will directly inform how the City understands its investment in arts, culture, heritage, and science.

Location: Vancouver, WA (Hybrid — Mix of in-person and remote work)
Duration and Hours: 10 hours per week across two consecutive semesters
Reports to: Inspire Vancouver Program Supervisor

Qualifications

Required

- Experience conducting surveys and/or gathering community input
- Experience creating reports from survey or research data (academic, professional, or volunteer experience all count)
- Strong written communication skills
- Interest in arts, culture, heritage, and/or science nonprofit organizations
- Comfort with common survey, spreadsheet, and presentation tools

Preferred

- Experience engaging diverse or historically underserved communities
- Bilingual skills (Spanish, Russian, Chuukese, Vietnamese, and other languages spoken in Vancouver are a plus)
- Familiarity with data visualization tools or qualitive and quantitative research methods
- Experience with community-based, participatory, or arts-based research

Qualifications

Scope of Work

Survey Design & Strategy

- Develop a survey and data collection strategy that reaches across Vancouver’s diverse communities, including residents, grantee organizations, and individual artists, historians, scientists, and cultural leaders.
- Design survey instruments that are culturally responsive: accessible, welcoming, and inclusive of different languages, traditions, and lived experiences.
- Use creative approaches to gathering input. Think beyond standard online forms such as in-person engagement at cultural events, partnership-based outreach, participatory or arts-based methods, plain-language and multilingual options.

Data Collection & Community Engagement

- Pilot and refine survey tools with support and guidance from the Inspire Vancouver team.
- Engage community members, grantees, and cultural practitioners in ways that build trust and encourage participation.
- Ensure data collection follows ethical and privacy best practices.
- Track participation and outreach efforts across different communities.

Analysis and Reporting

- Clean, organize, and analyze survey data.
- Create accessible reports and visual summaries that tell the story of the program’s impact.
- Help prepare materials for public audiences, the Culture, Arts, and Heritage Commission, and Vancouver City Council.
- Present findings to Inspire Vancouver staff and, as opportunities arise, to the Commission and City Council.

Educational Learning Objectives

By the end of this internship, you will be able to:

- Design culturally responsive research instruments – identify and apply methods for engaging historically underserved communities in civic and cultural research, including creative and participatory approaches.
- Conduct ethical community-based data collection – plan and execute a real-world survey project with multiple audiences, managing outreach, consent, privacy, and community relationships.
- Analyze and interpret real data – analyze survey responses, identify patterns and insights, and translate numbers into meaningful findings.
- Communicate data for public impact – produce clear written and visual reports tailored to community audiences, elected officials, and other stakeholders.
- Present to decision-makers – practice briefing city staff, commission members, and elected officials on your findings.
- Deepen knowledge of the arts, culture, heritage, and science sector – gain working knowledge of how a public cultural access program funds and supports local nonprofits, and how measurement supports public funding decisions.

Job Posting End Date

September 14, 2026

About Vital Lyfe

Vital Lyfe is a tech company redefining water autonomy through innovation, creating a new category of personal water making technology built to scale where infrastructure can’t.

The Mission
We're looking for a Software Engineering Intern to help build the software behind a high-demand consumer hardware product. We're spinning up manufacturing from scratch, scaling fast, and the software you work on will directly affect how we build, track, and deliver thousands of units.

You'll work alongside senior engineers on the tools, data systems, and infrastructure that power our operations and help us scale.

What You'll Do
• Build and improve internal tools that give our engineering and operations teams real-time visibility into production and manufacturing workflows
• Write integrations and scripts that connect systems and keep data reliable across the company
• Design and maintain dashboards that help teams understand operational data and make better decisions
• Assist with backend and cloud infrastructure work as we continue scaling our services
• Debug issues, write tests, and ship improvements alongside senior engineers

What We're Looking For
• Strong programming fundamentals and comfort learning new systems quickly
• Experience with at least one modern programming language such as Python or TypeScript
• Interest in software that supports real-world products and operations
• Familiarity with APIs, web applications, or cloud-based systems
• Practical and curious, with a habit of taking ownership and following through
• Able to break down a problem, work through it, and know when to ask for help
• Excited to work in a fast-paced environment where software and hardware intersect

Nice to Have
• Experience supporting or contributing to live backend systems
• Background in building user-facing interfaces with React or a similar frontend framework
• Exposure to SQL, structured data formats, and dashboards or data visualization tools
• Familiarity with AWS or cloud infrastructure
• Interest in manufacturing, hardware-software integration, or IoT systems

Why Join Vital Lyfe?
• Work on high-impact problems with global relevance
• Contribute to technology addressing water security and climate resilience
• Tackle meaningful problems at the intersection of software, hardware, and operations
• See your work directly affect how we build, ship, and improve real-world products
• Learn quickly in a collaborative environment with broad exposure across engineering

Internship Starts: Mid to Late September

Location Requirement: Ability to work 100% onsite in Torrance, CA (remote or hybrid work will not be considered)

Vital Lyfe is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Vital Lyfe is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Job Description

Are You Ready to Make It Happen at Mondelēz International?

Join our Mission to Lead the Future of Snacking. Make It Matter.

As an organization we are committed to developing the next generation of Makers and Bakers. Joining us at an early career stage in our fast paced and ever changing environment will enable you to do more, learn more and grow more. You will be encouraged to step outside your comfort zone– you may even surprise yourself! We will ensure you are given the support you need to be at your best and enable you to be yourself and bring passion and personality. Here you can lean in and speak up and bring your own flavor.

Mondelēz International was recognized as one of the Top 100 Intern Programs in the US in 2026 by Yello & WayUp and one of the Best Companies for New Graduates by Forbes.

Research & Development

In Research & Development, your skills can be the special ingredient that brings our brands to life. As part of a fantastic team of scientists, engineers, and nutritionists, you’ll work tirelessly on product design or development, process development, quality, nutrition, sensory and food safety aspects to ensure we deliver a consistent, delightful consumer experience. R&D is where you’ll turn great ideas into brilliant brands.

An internship within the R&D organization is a 10-to-12-week assignment providing real-world experiences in areas such as Research, Product Development, Process Development, Quality and Consumer Science

- Research - Internships consist of working on projects related to the development of technology to enhance existing products or enable future innovation.

- Product Development - Internships generally focus on product design to create new or improve existing products or work in other strategic focus areas for the company such as business continuity, sustainability, and Mindful Snacking (well-being).

- Process Development - Internships generally focus on the development of methods for converting raw materials into finished products, as well as continuous improvement of

- existing processes.

- Consumer Science- Internships consist of working on projects related to consumer-inspired design leveraging sensory and consumer insight tools and applications.

- Quality – Internships consist of projects that focus on driving the consistency and integrity of our products by ensuring all quality and safety standards are met.

- And other teams within R&D

We are looking for qualified individuals with a desire to work in the food industry and are interested in growing their problem solving and analytical skills in a real-life research and development environment. Leadership, innovative thoughts, and a strong desire to learn are critical to succeed.

Mondelēz International R&D Interns quickly learn through on-the-job experiences and are afforded the opportunity to work on substantial and meaningful projects that contribute to the business. Interns are provided with a network of mentors, peer and experts to aid in the development of their food technology and professional skills. Each intern is assigned a supervisor who designates projects and provides guidance. Team building and networking events are held throughout the summer with the intern class. Interns will be assessed, during their internship on overall performance, including functional skills, project management and personal leadership skills.

Requirements and Preferred Qualifications

- Pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in: Chemical Engineering (preferred) or Food Science (preferred) or other related fields.

- Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree with a preferred expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2029.

- Statistical Analysis (MiniTab, JMP, SAS, or similar statistical software/language)

- Analytical and computer skills (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)

- Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States and with Mondelēz International (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status.

Bonus to have experience with:

- Digital Tools:

- Python, R, PowerBI, Tableau, PowerApps, Quickbase, ANSYS, GPROMs, SQL, AutoCad, SolidWorks, or others.

- Modelling & Simulation:

- Computational Fluid Dynamics, Finite Element Analysis, Discrete Element Methods, Discrete Event Simulations, Process Modelling, Molecular Dynamics or Reaction Kinetics Modelling, Artificial intelligence, Data Modelling, Data Wrangling, Data Visualization, or others.

The ideal candidate displays some of the following characteristics:

- Strong leadership potential and student leadership experience.

- Excellent communication skills and resilience.

- Adaptable, with interpersonal savvy and engaged in diverse extracurricular activities.

- Demonstrating a growth mindset, agility, integrity, and a vision for the future.

- Strong cognitive abilities, willingness to learn, and data pattern recognition.

- Driven, curious, and ready to make a positive impact.

Why choose Mondelez International?

Ever wondered how your favorite snacks get made? Don’t miss the chance to find out! Check out some of the perks of being a MDLZ Intern:

- Subsidized, fully furnished housing for the Summer (For those who qualify)

- Roundtrip travel covered at the beginning and end of the internship

- Given value added projects that are presented to Leadership

- Intern programming, including events and activities throughout the summer

- Full-Time conversion opportunities upon graduation

Compensation

- The expected compensation weekly pay ranges for interns is $1,103 - $1,343 based on your expected graduation date.

- Compensation rates for Summer Interns is pre-determined and non-negotiable.
